bibl.title: Two Families and the Monetization of Arsinoite Villages in Roman Egypt.
bibl.seg: François Lerouxel, Two Families and the Monetization of Arsinoite Villages in Roman Egypt.
Oğuz Tekin (ed.), Second International Congress on the History of Money and Numismatics in the Mediterranean World, 5-8 January 2017, Antalya. Proceedings (Antalya, 2018) pp. 413-427.
bibl.note: 1. Introduction. - 2. Economic activities carried out in silver coins: a. The credit market; - b. Buying and selling land; - c. Patrimonial liturgies? - 3. Economic activities carried out in bronze coins: low-level taxation mainly: a. Taxation in cash paid in bronze coins and recorded in the silver standard; - b. Taxation in cash paid in bronze coins and recorded in the bronze standard. - 4. Economic activities carried out in kind: cereal agriculture mostly: a. Inputs in cereal agriculture: agricultural labor and seed; - b. Outputs in cereal agriculture: rents, taxation, and consumption; - c. Liturgies. - Conclusion. - [Focuses on two family archives from Tebtynis: Philosarapis and Kronion.]
